paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of Micah 2. Power is not permission. The people in this passage lay in bed and plotted evil, and Micah says they carried it out "because the power is in their hands." They took fields and homes, and they took a man's inheritance (Micah 2:1-2). The LORD notices when the strong squeeze the weak, and He says so out loud.

Notice something else, baker. The very people grabbing fields said, "Do not preach," and told themselves that disgrace would not overtake them (Micah 2:6). Then the LORD says a man of wind with a wine sermon would be "just the preacher for this people!" (Micah 2:11). Friend, that's the real danger. We can get so comfortable that we only want to hear what feels good. I'd rather hear the hard word from the LORD than a pleasant lie I can't bake anything with.

But the passage doesn't end in the dark, and I'm so glad. The LORD says, "I will surely gather all of you, O Jacob; I will collect the remnant of Israel" (Micah 2:12). "Their King will pass through before them, the LORD as their leader" (Micah 2:13). Friend, He doesn't just correct His people, He goes out in front of them. So take the hard word, let it do its work, and follow the One who leads the way.
